delete.title: Delete VAT rate - {{entry}}
delete.label: Delete
delete.confirm: Deleting a rate is permanent. The previous row for the same country and class takes its period back. Orders and invoices already written keep their own rate. Are you sure?

help.intro: A row says what percentage a VAT class carries in a country from a given day - RO, Reduced, 11%, from 2025-08-01. A product declares a class, never a percentage; the percentage is looked up here when a cart or the catalog is priced, at the rates of the shop's own country.
help.step_1_title: A rate change is one new row
help.step_1_body: Rows have a start day and no end: the rate in force on a day is the row with the newest start day on or before it. To apply a new law, add a row dated the day it takes effect. A future day is fine - the new rate takes over on its own at midnight, company time, and the old row keeps covering every day before it.
help.step_2_body: Standard, Reduced and Second reduced carry a percentage and are stored here. Zero-rated and Exempt are 0% everywhere and have no rows. A class a country has no row for is priced at that country's Standard rate - over-charging VAT is the safer error - and a country with no Standard rate in force refuses to price at all until one is added.
help.step_3_body: Only the rate and the notes are editable. The country, the class and the start day identify the row, so a row entered for the wrong one is deleted and entered again. A correction reaches carts and catalog prices; deleting a row hands its period back to the row before it.
help.step_4_body: An order line and an invoice line freeze the rate they were priced at, so nothing changed here moves an order, an invoice or a report already written. The list orders by start day, country or id, newest first; filter by class, or search an id or the notes from three characters.
help.note: Romania's rates from 2017 on are inserted when the database is migrated. Check each new law against the class mapping before adding its row: a dish's class is set on the product, not here.
